blocks.text: Landing page cost in 2026 sits between €2,500 and €5,000 for a professionally built launch site. Recent webvise offers for exactly this artifact ran between **€2,500 and €4,900, fixed price**, and the average project shipped in about three weeks.
German studios publish entry prices of €6,500 for the same job.

You want a number before you book a call, and most agency pricing pages refuse to give one. This article publishes the range from webvise's recent offers, the six scope drivers that move a quote, and the market prices to compare against. Every figure comes from a delivered project or an offer webvise actually sent, stated as a range wherever a client is involved.

items: **Recent webvise fixed-price offers** for launch and company sites ran between €2,500 and €4,900. The entry anchor is €2,500.
**Three weeks is the average build time** across 25+ delivered projects. A 61-page bilingual rebuild took one day; a 7-language 3D site took 4 weeks.
**Six scope drivers set the price:** page count, languages, content migration versus new copy, forms and integrations, accessibility, and 3D or motion.
**The market comparison:** H-Studio Berlin publishes websites from €6,500, Berlin MVP builds start at €18,000. webvise sits below both because AI-native delivery cuts build hours.
**Real scope lists** included bilingual content migration, image optimization from 464 MB to 42 MB, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, analytics, and a QA pass with zero console errors.

blocks.text: If your scope is already clear, [webvise's landing page service](/services/landing-pages) lists what a fixed-price build includes, starting at €2,500. The rest of this article shows how that number moves.
The Real Range: €2,500 to €4,900
Recent webvise offers for launch and company sites ran between €2,500 and €4,900. Each one was a fixed price agreed before the build started, so the invoice held even when the work ran long.
€2,500 is the honest entry anchor for a professional build.
The money buys concrete line items. These come from real webvise scope lists, so treat them as the minimum a serious quote should itemize:

items: **Bilingual content migration.** Existing pages move into the new site in two languages, cleaned up along the way.
**Image optimization.** One project's media library shrank from 464 MB to 42 MB before launch.
**Accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA.** The German BFSG has applied to consumer-facing digital services since June 2025, so this is a legal line item.
**Analytics set up before launch.** The first campaign produces data from day one.
**A QA pass with zero console errors.** Every page loads clean before handover.

Three Weeks Is the Average, With Outliers in Both Directions

webvise has delivered 25+ projects at a 3-week average to launch. The average holds because delivery is AI-native: webvise.io itself is 100% AI-coded via Claude Code, and client builds run through the same tooling. [The full workflow is documented on this blog](/blog/ai-powered-development-workflow).
The fast outlier is a 61-page bilingual site rebuilt in one day with that tooling. The scope was pure migration: content existed in both languages, no new copy, no 3D.
The slow outlier is Old World Labs: 7 languages and custom 3D pushed the build to 4 weeks. Both drivers were visible before the first line of code, and so was the extra week.
Where the Range Sits in the German Market

H-Studio Berlin publishes websites from €6,500. Berlin studios offer MVP builds from €18,000, a different artifact with application logic inside. Both are honest published prices for classic delivery models.

rows: Custom landing or company site, about 3 weeks

blocks.text: A lower price has to come from fewer hours or thinner scope, and any vendor should tell you which. For webvise the answer is public: AI-native delivery cuts build hours while the scope list stays the same. That claim is checkable, the studio's own site is the proof.
When the Budget Question Is Bigger Than a Landing Page

A landing page budget answers one narrow question: what it costs to put one offer online fast. Once the project needs a login area, checkout, dashboards, or an application workflow, the artifact changes and the range moves with it. The broader guide, [how much does a website cost in 2026](/blog/how-much-does-a-website-cost), applies the same range logic to full websites and platforms.

webvise builds landing pages and launch sites at a fixed price, most of them live within three weeks. Send your offer and your driver count via [the contact form](/#contact), and a fixed number comes back itemized against the six drivers above.
